subject: Confirming TTFT SLOs & streaming packetization for Nimble pilot
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimblecommerce.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@nimblecommerce.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming TTFT SLOs & streaming packetization for Nimble pilot

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciate the level of detail on rendering constraints and peak traffic patterns. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can align the pilot and contracting path.

Key performance targets you asked us to validate:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token / first-byte): target median ~120–180 ms; p95 < 300 ms; p99 aim < 500 ms.
- Streaming model: browser clients will stream partial responses to the UI. You prefer SSE as the primary transport with WebSocket as a fallback for mobile SDK multiplexing.
- Chunk cadence & packetization: preference for chunky updates sized ~80–150 tokens (roughly 250–600ms of generated text depending on model) to avoid layout jank. You emphasized first-chunk arrival (first meaningful token) over total response latency.
- Throughput/concurrency: production steady-state estimate ~60 concurrent open streams (users), daily peak bursts up to ~350 qps for short periods; typical response payloads ~250–400 tokens.

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot:
1) A short pilot config (2–4 weeks) instrumented for TTFT measurement at our edge and via a small client-side SDK to capture user-perceived first-chunk timing.
2) Two config templates: latency-optimized (aggressive batching limits, higher cost) and cost-optimized (larger batching windows, prefix caching). We’ll run canonical load tests for both.
3) Acceptance criteria: median TTFT within agreed band, p95 under the negotiated threshold for 48-hour rolling windows, and streaming chunk cadence consistency (95% of chunks < X ms inter-chunk gap — to be defined below).

Open items / asks from you before we start:
- Confirm the hard p95 target you want us to guarantee for the pilot (I proposed 300 ms).
- Provide a representative prompt set (10–20 prompts) and a small sample of typical user session patterns (burst profile + steady-state).
- Procurement contact for contracting and any PO timelines.

Attached a short pilot SLO proposal and our TTFT playbook. Propose a 30-minute technical alignment next week (available Tue/Thu 9–11 PT).

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock down requirements:  

1) Chunk cadence: when you say "95% of chunks < X ms inter-chunk gap", can you be more concrete about how Redwood defines the inter-chunk gap? We render progressively and we need predictable inter-chunk timing to avoid UI reflow. Is this measured at our edge, at the model process, or at the browser SDK?

2) First-chunk vs first-byte: our product team cares more about "first meaningful token" (first chunk that contains user-visible prose) rather than the first binary byte — are those distinct in your telemetry?

3) For throughput: our capacity planning needs a sense of how concurrent open streams translate to QPS for your runtime (i.e., 60 concurrent streams — what qps range should we expect for the pilot?).

Procurement is looped in (procure@nimblecommerce.com) — they’ll start the paperwork once we agree on pilot SLOs.

Can we do the tech alignment on Tue 9:30 PT?

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confirming TTFT SLOs & streaming packetization for Nimble pilot

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers inline below and a suggested pilot configuration.

1) How we measure inter-chunk gap:
- We measure inter-chunk gap both at our edge (time between the TCP/HTTP chunk deliveries leaving our edge) and via SDK instrumentation in the browser (time between visible tokens). For contract-level SLOs we recommend agreeing on edge-observed metrics (reliable and server-controlled) while using SDK telemetry for user-perceived validation.

2) First-chunk vs first-byte:
- We distinguish: TTFT-first-byte is the moment any token/byte leaves the edge; TTFT-first-meaningful is a higher-level event we can compute using heuristics on the generation stream (e.g., drop leading punctuation/metadata tokens). For the pilot we can provide both telemetry streams. Our recommendation: guarantee first-meaningful median <= 200 ms and p95 <= 350 ms for the latency-optimized config.

3) Concurrency -> QPS mapping:
- In your profile (60 steady-state open streams) that maps to ~60 concurrent requests if each stream triggers a single in-flight generation. If you use progressive pagination (multiple small requests per user), qps will be higher. For planning assume 60–120 qps steady with bursts to 350 qps for 30–90s windows depending on client behavior. We’ll run the surge test during pilot.

Pilot configuration (recommended):
- Duration: 3 weeks (14-day ramp + 7-day steady validation)
- Load: synthetic client sim with 60 steady concurrent streams, burst scripts to 350 qps, average response size 300 tokens.
- Acceptance: latency-optimized config must hit median first-meaningful <= 200 ms and p95 <= 350 ms across a 72-hour rolling window.
- Fallbacks: SSE primary with optional WebSocket for mobile. We’ll instrument an adaptive chunking shim that aims for 80–120 token chunks but will adjust for model latency to keep inter-chunk gap < 400 ms for 95% of chunks.

Next steps:
- Laura / Ben: I’ve attached the pilot SLO doc. Can you help produce a short list of 10 representative prompts and a small client-side trace sample?
- Elena / Procurement: please confirm the PO timeline. If procurement can start the paperwork we can lock dates.

I’m good for Tue 9:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Markus
